goals.0: 10 new words, each with its pronunciation
goals.1: A short dialogue: tap each word to compare it with the Bangla and English
goals.2: Verb forms: ich komme, du kommst
dialog.0.de.1.n: Question word; it comes at the start of the sentence
dialog.0.de.3.n: Use du with friends and people your age; Sie with older people you don't know
dialog.1.de.0.n: Pronoun; written with a lowercase i in the middle of a sentence
dialog.1.de.1.n: Add -e to the verb after ich
dialog.1.de.4.n: „Und du?“ = And you? — a very common short question
dialog.2.de.1.n: sein is irregular: ich bin, du bist, er ist. In Bangla, “I (am) Muna” needs no verb
dialog.2.de.3.n: One word for “where … from”, which English splits into two parts
dialog.2.de.4.n: Add -st to the verb after du
dialog.2.de.5.n: In a question the verb comes first, then du
dialog.3.de.1.n: The verb is in second place; in Bangla it comes at the end
dialog.3.de.2.n: aus shows that you come from a country or city
dialog.3.de.5.n: Add -e after ich; “w” is pronounced like English “v”
dialog.3.de.6.n: Bangla puts this as an ending on the noun (Dhaka + -y)
dialog.4.de.0.n: ö sound: say “e” with rounded lips
grammar.0.intro: In Bangla the verb ending changes with the subject (“ami ashi, tumi asho, she ashe” = I come, you come, he/she comes), and German does the same. Drop -en from the infinitive and add the ending.
grammar.0.note: heißen already has ß in the stem, so du only adds -t: du heißt. And sein (to be) is irregular: ich bin, du bist, er ist.
grammar.1.title: The verb comes second
grammar.1.text: In Bangla the verb comes at the end of the sentence; in a normal German sentence the verb is always in second position.
quiz.0.why: heißen = to be called. Ich heiße Saheb = My name is Saheb.
quiz.2.why: After ich the verb ends in -e: ich komme.
quiz.4.prompt: Put the words in order: “Where are you from?”
quiz.4.why: Question word first, then the verb, then du.
quiz.5.prompt: The correct form of heißen with du
quiz.5.why: The stem already ends in ß, so du only adds -t: du heißt.
quiz.6.why: The verb is in second place and takes -e after ich: Ich wohne in Dhaka.
